correctness.rationale: Every pair of distinct vertices in a connected complete multipartite graph is at distance one across parts and distance two within a part. Hence p=0 imposes no restriction, p=1 means independence and thus one-part support, and p at least two forces a singleton. Independently, d=0 forces the whole vertex set, d=1 is ordinary domination, and d at least two makes every nonempty set dominating. The eight polynomial cases are exactly the Cartesian combination of these structural facts. Exhaustive direct distance checking through order eight and d,p through four matches every coefficient.

value.rationale: A natural complete classification can be valuable even when its proof is short. The recent literature studies the two-parameter invariant on paths, cycles, trees, and graph products; the complete multipartite family is a canonical diameter-two test class. The result resolves every parameter pair and counts every feasible set, exposing exactly where nonexistence occurs and how the modern parameter collapses onto classical domination notions. This is more informative than a routine single-number substitution.
